headline: Premium spend and credit strength lift profit growth
summary_short: American Express's Q2 2026 contract revenue (ex-net interest income) rose 8.6% y/y to $11.21B, and diluted EPS rose 11% to $4.53, as billed business grew 9% and credit-loss provisions fell 23% q/q to $1.08B on a reserve release.
summary_long: Revenue from contracts with customers (SEC XBRL basis; excludes net interest income) rose 8.6% y/y to $11.21B. Net income rose 7.8% y/y to $3.11B; diluted EPS rose 11% to $4.53, matching AmEx's disclosed growth rate. Billed business grew 9% y/y on broad Goods & Services and Travel & Entertainment strength; net card fees grew 15% on new-card acquisitions. Provisions for credit losses fell 23% q/q to $1.08B on a reserve release versus a prior-period reserve build, as delinquencies fell to 1.2%. CET1 held at 10.4%, within the 10-11% target range; AmEx returned $2.9B to shareholders via buybacks and dividends. Cash fell to $45.2B from $53.8B q/q. No full-year EPS/revenue guidance in this filing; FY2026 funding plan targets $4.0-8.0B unsecured debt.

drivers.explanation: Card Member spend and revenue momentum, excellent credit performance and disciplined expense management together drove the quarter's results, per management commentary.
Discount revenue grew on 9% billed-business growth; net card fees grew 15% on new-card acquisitions and retention; net interest income grew 11% on balance growth and net yield expansion.
EPS growth outpaced net income growth because diluted shares outstanding fell to 679M from 699M a year ago on continued buybacks.
